Community-weighted mean traits

Source: R/traits.R
trait_cwm.Rd

The abundance-weighted mean of each numeric trait in each site, and the abundance-weighted proportion of each level of categorical traits (Garnier et al. 2004; de Bello et al. 2021, ch. 5). Species with a missing trait value are left out of that trait's mean, and the weights of the remaining species are rescaled.

Usage

trait_cwm(
  data,
  traits,
  site = site,
  species = species,
  abundance = NULL,
  cols = tidyselect::everything()
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in long format, with one row per record.

traits

A data frame of traits, one row per species, with a column whose name matches the species column of data.

site, species

<tidy-select> The column holding site identifiers and the column holding species names.

abundance

<tidy-select> The column holding counts. If NULL (the default), a column called abundance is used when present, otherwise every row counts as one individual.

cols

<tidy-select> Trait columns of traits.

Value

A tibble with one row per site and trait: the site column, trait and cwm. Site variables (constant within sites) are kept.

References

Garnier, E. et al. (2004). Plant functional markers capture ecosystem properties during secondary succession. Ecology, 85, 2630-2637. doi:10.1890/03-0799

Examples

aravo <- data_aravo()
trait_cwm(aravo$community, aravo$traits, abundance = cover)
#> # A tibble: 600 × 9
#>    site  trait    cwm Aspect Slope Form  PhysD ZoogD  Snow

#>  6 AR06  Height  6.93      8    20 3        40 high    160
